==English==
[[File:Freestyle swimming2.gif|thumb|A freestyle swimming stroke animation]]

===Pronunciation===
{{commonscat}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈswɪmɪŋ/}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-swimming.ogg|a=US}}
*** {{IPA|en|/ˈswɪmiŋ/|a=Upper Midwestern US,Western US,CA,pre-/ŋ/-tensing}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪmɪŋ|s=2}}
* {{hyph|en|swim|ming}}

===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|en|enm|swymmynge}}. Equivalent to {{affix|en|swim|t1=to move through water|pos1=verb|-ing|id2=gerund noun|pos2=suffix forming gerunds}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# The act or art of [[sustain]]ing and [[propel]]ling the body in water.
#: {{ux|en|Triathlon competitors take part in open water '''swimming'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1909|author=Swami Rama Tirtha|title=In Woods of God-realization: The pole star within|edition=7th
|passage=The daring adventures of the American people in their scalings of the Alps and the Rocky mountains and in their '''swimmings''' across the Niagara rapids {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Bonnie Tsui|title=The Self-Reflecting Pool|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/02/15/opinion/sunday/the-self-reflecting-pool.html|date=2014-02-14|passage=Though we don’t all reach nirvana when we swim, '''swimming''' may well be that last refuge from connectivity — and, for some, the only way to find the solitary self.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210815174721/https://www.nytimes.com/2014/02/15/opinion/sunday/the-self-reflecting-pool.html}}

===Etymology 2===
{{ety|en|:af|swim<t:to be dizzy><pos:verb>|-ing<pos:suffix forming gerunds><id:gerund noun>|text=+|tree=1}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# The state of being [[dizzy]] or in [[vertigo]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1624|location=London|publisher=Richard Field|author=Philip Barrough|title=The Method of Physick, Contaning the Cavses, Signes, and Cvres of Inward Diseases in Mans Body, From the Head to the Foote:{{nb...}}|edition=6th|page=134|pageurl=https://hdl.handle.net/2027/uc1.31378008344437?urlappend=%3Bseq=164|text=But when the worms are killed with the aforesaid medicines, you must driue them out without delay : for there proceedeth a vicious exhalation from them, which both destroyeth appetite, and hurteth digestion, and being lifted vpward, it causeth '''swimmings''', and other euils.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1640|location=London|author=John Parkinson|title=Theatrum Botanicum: The Theater of Plants. Or, an Herball of Large Extent:{{nb...}}|page=552|pageurl=https://hdl.handle.net/2027/ucm.5326186314?urlappend=%3Bseq=576|text=[The Speedwell] doth also wonderfully helpe the memory, and to ease all turnings and '''swimmings''', and other paines of the head, and as it is sayd helpeth women to become fruitfull, that were barren[.]}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1869|author=William Chambers; Robert Chambers|title=Chambers's Miscellany of Instructive & Entertaining Tracts|page=2
|passage='''Swimmings''' of the head and intestinal pains seemed the prelude of dissolution.}}
